You are the Recovery Auditor in RecoveryPact.

Two guardians negotiated a database recovery: the Database Guardian (restore the database)
and the Continuity Guardian (protect the business). An independent authority decided what
could run and an independent verifier judged whether the business recovered.

Your job, after the fact:
1. Write a short post-incident report for the owning team: what broke, what was decided and
   why, what happened, and whether the business is back. Plain language, numbers from the
   trace, no speculation beyond the evidence.
2. Extract at most 3 lessons that would make the NEXT negotiation on the same workload
   faster or safer. A good lesson is specific (names the workload), actionable (what to do
   or check first) and grounded in what happened. Do not repeat generic policy.
3. Judge the negotiation itself: did either guardian waste a round, miss evidence, or get
   overridden by an invariant?

Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose.

{
  "report": "Checkout degraded to 50% success (vs 95% SLO) with $9,200/min revenue at risk due to 10-12 sessions blocked by an idle-in-transaction batch_replayable_inventory worker (pid 104009/104368). The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker; the Continuity Guardian initially requested change-calendar evidence (Invariant I2), which confirmed no active window. After a first contract was denied due to a stale blocker PID (live_identity check), a second negotiation terminated the new blocker (pid 104368) in one round. Verification confirmed full recovery: 100% checkout success over 10s, no lock waits, and no protected settlements aborted. Total incident duration was ~116 seconds.",
  "root_cause": "An idle-in-transaction batch_replayable_inventory job (inventory_reconcile) held locks that blocked checkout sessions, degrading success to 50% and risking $9,200/min in revenue.",
  "lessons": [
    "For batch_replayable_inventory (inventory_reconcile): add a pre-negotiation check that fetches change-calendar evidence automatically so the Continuity Guardian never has to request it in round 1.",
    "For batch_replayable_inventory (inventory_reconcile): implement a statement/transaction timeout (e.g., 30s) so idle-in-transaction workers self-terminate before they become root blockers.",
    "For batch_replayable_inventory (inventory_reconcile): cache the workload registry + change-calendar snapshot at negotiation start to avoid a renegotiation loop when the blocker PID changes mid-incident."
  ],
  "negotiation_critique": "The Database Guardian acted correctly but wasted round 1 of the first negotiation by not including change-calendar evidence upfront, forcing a revision. The Continuity Guardian correctly enforced Invariant I2. The authority's live_identity check correctly caught the stale PID, but the renegotiation repeated the same evidence gathering instead of reusing the cached registry/calendar data.",
  "follow_ups": [
    "Add a statement_timeout (e.g., 30s) to the batch_worker role or the inventory_reconcile job to prevent idle-in-transaction lock holding.",
    "Instrument the orchestrator to pre-fetch and attach change-calendar evidence for any BATCH_REPLAYABLE workload when a termination is first proposed.",
    "Update the authority's live_identity check to allow PID migration within the same application_name if the workload registry confirms replayability, avoiding a full renegotiation."
  ]
}
